zh.title: 空中巴士與法國航空成立合資公司 Alpha Component Solutions 專責A350零組件維修
zh.summary: 空中巴士與法國航空成立合資公司；專責A350零組件維修；涵蓋逾500架飛機
body: 空中巴士（Airbus）於2026年10月28日宣佈，已與法國航空（Air France）正式成立持股比例各佔50%的合資企業「Alpha Component Solutions」，專門為A350長程廣體客機提供航材零組件支援服務。新實體旨在協助全球營運商維修關鍵零組件，並維持機隊可用性。
該合資實體由空中巴士與法航荷航集團（Air France-KLM）共同營運，負責管理全球共享存取零組件庫。這項合作將為全球空中巴士A350客戶提供包含飛機零組件資產、維修服務、供應鏈管理以及零件修理等全方位後勤支援。
透過結合空中巴士飛行小時服務（FHS）與法航荷航航太維修（AFI KLM E&M）的綜合能力，該合資企業針對全球A350機隊日益增長的長期零組件維修需求提供優化方案。合資公司目前在合約上已支援超過500架飛機，並擁有支援全球新舊營運商的服務網絡。
法航荷航工程與維修執行副總裁Anne Brachet表示，獲得可靠的零組件對於維持機隊可用性與營運績效至關重要。她指出，將第一線航空公司營運經驗與空中巴士的FHS能力結合後，Alpha Component Solutions將為客戶提供更廣泛的支援網絡與客製化解決方案。
空中巴士商用飛機客戶服務高級副總裁Cristina Aguilar Grieder表示，該合資公司代表著大幅提升A350零組件支援的重要一步，匯集了空中巴士與法航荷航航太維修的專業知識與資源，致力於為全球客戶提供最佳化的維修解決方案。
空中巴士補充說明，該合資企業結合營運卓越與進階供應鏈能力，以提升零組件可靠性、簡化生命週期維修，並提供客製化支援，從而強化全球營運商的長期營運韌性。

en.title: Airbus and Air France Finalize Joint Venture Alpha Component Solutions for A350 Fleet Support
en.summary: Airbus and Air France finalize joint venture Alpha Component Solutions to provide global A350 component support.
body: Airbus announced on 28 October 2026 that it has officially finalised the establishment of 'Alpha Component Solutions', a 50-50 joint venture created with Air France to deliver dedicated component support for the Airbus A350 long-range widebody aircraft family. The newly created entity will assist global operators in maintaining fleet availability and servicing critical aircraft components.

The new entity will be operated jointly between Airbus and Air France-KLM to manage a worldwide shared-access pool. The collaboration is structured to provide comprehensive aircraft component assets, maintenance services, supply chain management, and repair capabilities for global Airbus A350 customers.

By leveraging the combined capabilities of Airbus' Flight Hours Services (FHS) and Air France Industries KLM Engineering & Maintenance (AFI KLM E&M), the joint venture provides an enhanced solution to address the expanding long-term component maintenance requirements of the global A350 fleet. The enterprise already contractually supports more than 500 aircraft with a worldwide footprint ready to serve operators.

Anne Brachet, Executive Vice President of Air France-KLM Engineering & Maintenance, stated that reliable access to components is essential for maintaining fleet availability and operational performance. She highlighted that combining firsthand airline operational experience with Airbus' FHS capabilities allows Alpha Component Solutions to deliver a broader support network tailored to airline needs.

Cristina Aguilar Grieder, Senior Vice President of Customer Services Commercial Aircraft at Airbus, noted that the strategic partnership represents a major step forward in enhancing A350 aftermarket support by uniting the expertise and resources of both companies to deliver optimised solutions worldwide.

Airbus indicated that the joint venture combines operational excellence with advanced supply chain capabilities to drive higher component reliability, streamline lifecycle maintenance, and deliver tailored support to bolster long-term operational resilience for airlines.

zh.title: 波音公佈2026年第三季財報 營收242億美元淨虧損收窄至1.16億
zh.summary: 波音公佈2026年第三季財報；淨虧損收窄至1.16億美元；737-7與737-10獲認證
body: 波音（Boeing）於2026年10月27日公佈2026年第三季財務業績。受惠於國防與服務業務強勁表現，波音該季度營收同比增長4%至242億美元。在財務表現方面，波音第三季淨虧損為1.16億美元，相較於去年同期因777X專案大額計提而導致的53億美元淨虧損大幅收窄。截至該季度末，波音總積壓訂單金額創下7450億美元的歷史新高紀錄。
在民用客機監管與認證進展方面，波音於第三季取得重要關鍵里程碑。旗下737 MAX系列中兩款尚未完成認證的衍生機型均已順利取得執照。其中，737-7機型在第三季獲得美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）頒發的修訂型別認證，而機身較長的737-10機型則隨後於2026年10月取得認證許可。這意味著737 MAX家族中的剩餘機型已正式完成主管機關的法規認證程序。
商用飛機部門在第三季實現營收107億美元，營運虧損為6.97億美元。交機數據顯示，波音於第三季共交付161架商用飛機，高於去年同期的160架，使2026年前九個月的累積交付總量達到475架。在第三季交付的飛機中，主要以單走道737系列客機為主，該季度共計交付124架。目前737專案正朝向每月47架的穩定生產速率努力，而787客機家族則維持每月8架的穩定產率。
在新機訂單與市場需求方面，波音商用飛機部門在第三季錄得300架淨訂單，主要訂購客戶包含土耳其航空（Turkish Airlines）、衣索比亞航空（Ethiopian Airlines）以及漢莎航空（Lufthansa）。受惠於新訂單挹注，波音商用飛機部門的積壓訂單總量已超過6,300架，總價值估算達創紀錄的6120億美元，顯示出航空公司客戶對波音商用客機產品線的強勁需求。
在國防、太空與安全部門方面，波音該季度表現顯著提升，營收年增15%至79億美元，營運利潤成長至4.92億美元。在該季度內，美國海軍選定波音負責設計、製造並交付其F/A-XX下一代戰鬥機。此外，波音環球服務部門營收成長4%至56億美元，並取得美國陸軍AH-64阿帕契直升機隊的維護合約，截至季度末積壓訂單金額達330億美元。

en.title: Boeing Reports Q3 2026 Results as Loss Narrows to $116M and 737 MAX Variants Win Certification
en.summary: Boeing reports Q3 2026 net loss narrows to $116 million as 737-7 and 737-10 secure certification.
body: Boeing reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 on October 27, 2026, posting a 4% year-on-year increase in total quarterly revenue to $24.2 billion, driven mainly by stronger performance across its defense and services divisions. The aircraft manufacturer recorded a net loss of $116 million for the period, marking a substantial reduction from the $5.3 billion loss recorded during the same period a year earlier, when operations were hit by charges on the 777X program. Driven by continued customer demand, Boeing closed the third quarter with a total company backlog reaching a record $745 billion.

The third quarter marked major regulatory milestones for Boeing's commercial aircraft line, with both remaining 737 MAX variants securing key approvals. The 737-7 received amended type certification from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) during the third quarter, and the larger 737-10 model achieved its certification in October 2026. Executive Chief Kelly Ortberg noted that these certification milestones reflect important progress as the manufacturer continues to focus on safety, operational quality, and disciplined execution.

Boeing Commercial Airplanes recorded third-quarter revenue of $10.7 billion with an operating loss of $697 million, impacted by delivery mix and projected costs related to production rate adjustments. The commercial division delivered 161 airplanes during the third quarter, up from 160 delivered a year earlier, bringing commercial deliveries for the first nine months of 2026 to 475 aircraft. Deliveries were led by the single-aisle 737 family, which accounted for 124 aircraft handed over during the quarter. The 737 program is working toward a stable monthly production rate of 47 aircraft, while the 787 program remains stable at eight per month.

Commercial order activity remained robust throughout the third quarter, with Boeing booking 300 net commercial orders. Major international carriers placing orders during the quarter included Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines, and Lufthansa. This order momentum lifted Boeing's commercial backlog to over 6,300 aircraft, valued at a record $612 billion. Furthermore, certification flight testing for the 777-9 aircraft continued during the quarter, with Boeing confirming that the 777X program remains on track for its initial customer delivery in 2027.

Boeing Defense, Space & Security posted third-quarter revenue of $7.9 billion, representing a 15% increase, while operating earnings reached $492 million. During the quarter, the U.S. Navy selected Boeing to design, build, and deliver its F/A-XX next-generation fighter aircraft. Meanwhile, Boeing Global Services generated $5.6 billion in quarterly revenue with an 18.3% operating margin, securing a U.S. Army contract to support the AH-64 Apache fleet and ending the quarter with a $33 billion order backlog.

zh.title: 美國貿易代表警告空中巴士34億美元貸款威脅飛機貿易休戰
zh.summary: 美國指貸款注入不確定性；空中巴士稱屬標準融資
body: 美國貿易代表傑米森·格里爾於2026年10月26日發表聲明，質疑歐洲投資銀行對空中巴士的融資支持。
歐洲投資銀行早前批准高達30億歐元（約34億美元）貸款，用於空中巴士在法、德、西三國的研發。
格里爾表示：「這種情況給跨大西洋航空航天貿易注入了重大不確定性」；空中巴士回應稱貸款屬「標準企業融資安排」，並願與相關機構分享更多資訊。
美歐於2021年6月同意暫停因飛機補貼爭端產生的關稅五年，並設立工作組處理分歧；波音曾在2026年7月要求特朗普政府就該貸款尋求更多資訊。

en.title: US Trade Representative warns $3.4 billion Airbus loan threatens aircraft trade truce
en.summary: US says Airbus loan adds uncertainty; Airbus calls it standard financing
body: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer issued a statement on 26 October 2026 challenging the European Investment Bank’s support for Airbus.
The bank approved financing of up to €3 billion, approximately $3.4 billion, earlier this year for Airbus research and development in France, Germany and Spain.

Greer said the situation “injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector.” Airbus defended the loan, telling Reuters it was a “standard corporate financing facility” comparable to prior commercial loans and said it was willing to share more information.

The United States and the European Union agreed in June 2021 to suspend tariffs from their aircraft subsidy dispute for five years and set up a working group; Boeing had asked the Trump administration in July 2026 to seek more information about the loan, Reuters reported.
